headline: Linux kernel developers are planning to drop the rule that code written with AI help must carry an "Assisted-by" tag.
score_reason: Lowered one point from 6: only the Phoronix headline could be read, so the details and the reasons are unverified.
importance_line: A change to how the Linux kernel, the core of the widely used Linux operating system, labels AI-assisted code would matter to software developers and to companies that depend on the kernel, but the exact rule, the reasons and who decides are not yet known.
summary: Phoronix reports that Linux kernel developers plan to remove the requirement that contributions made with the help of AI or large language models (the software behind AI chatbots) carry an "Assisted-by" tag.
notes: Headline only: Phoronix page blocked (HTTP 403, tried twice), no other outlet found. Score lowered 6 to 5 for being unverified.
